description: instinctagents - A two-part Skill & agents.md registry: a single-binary Rust CLI with TUI for installing/removing cataloged skills + agents.md snippets in any project, plus an agentic internal tool for maintainers to ingest entries from GitHub URLs into the registry repo. Supports Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode harnesses.

userStories.title: Create registry repo directory layout
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the registry repo to have the canonical folder layout so all subsequent code has a stable place to write to.
acceptanceCriteria: Top-level folders exist: skills/, agents.md/, src/internal/, src/external/, .github/workflows/
Top-level mapping.yml exists with empty lists: installed_skills: [], installed_agents_md: []
Root README.md explains registry purpose, curl install command (placeholder URL), basic usage
.gitignore excludes /target, *.tmp, build artifacts
Example skill skills/example-skill/ exists with SKILL.md and manifest.yml (placeholder content ok)
Example agents.md integration agents.md/example-integration/ exists with snippet.md and manifest.yml
mapping.yml references both example entries so catalog is non-empty
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Define and document manifest.yml schema
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a documented, validated schema for each skill and agents.md integration's manifest.yml so the build process and tools can rely on its shape.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/manifest-schema.md documents every field with name, type, required/optional, example, description
Required fields documented: name (string, must match folder name), description (string), version (semver string)
Optional fields documented: harness_compatibility (array of claude-code/codex/opencode; empty/omitted means all)
Skill manifests documented to support optional entrypoint (string, default SKILL.md)
agents.md manifests documented to support optional snippet_file (string, default snippet.md)
Example manifest files for both skill and agents.md integration included in the doc
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: docs/manifest-schema.md created with full field reference, validation rules, and example manifests for both skills and agents.md integrations.

userStories.title: Define and document mapping.yml schema
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a documented schema for mapping.yml so the internal tool's scripts can produce and consume it deterministically.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/mapping-schema.md documents mapping.yml's structure
Top-level keys documented: installed_skills (list), installed_agents_md (list)
Each entry documented with fields: name, version, source_url, install_path (e.g. skills/example-skill/)
Example valid mapping.yml included in the doc
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: docs/mapping-schema.md created documenting top-level keys (installed_skills, installed_agents_md), per-entry fields (name, version, source_url, install_path), validation rules, and example mapping.yml.

userStories.title: Cargo project setup with module skeleton
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a working Cargo project with module structure so subsequent stories have a clear place to add code.
acceptanceCriteria: src/external/Cargo.toml with package name instinctagents, edition 2021, binary target
Standalone or workspace layout (recommend workspace so internal Python lives in src/internal/ without polluting Cargo)
Module skeleton under src/external/src/: main.rs, cli.rs, tui.rs, harness.rs, catalog.rs, installer.rs, state.rs, update.rs, http.rs
cargo check passes
cargo build --release produces a binary
cargo clippy -- -D warnings passes

userStories.title: Build script bakes catalog metadata into binary
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the catalog (list of all skill and agents.md manifests) embedded into the binary at compile time so the tool works offline for browsing.
acceptanceCriteria: src/external/build.rs walks skills/*/manifest.yml and agents.md/*/manifest.yml from repo root
All manifests aggregated into a single structure exposed via generated .rs file in OUT_DIR (include! style)
Aggregate has two sections: skills and agents_md; each entry has name, description, version, harness_compatibility, source_path
Missing/malformed manifest causes build failure with a clear error identifying the offending file
Unit test verifies embedded catalog is non-empty and contains the example entries from US-001
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)

userStories.title: Harness detection module
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the tool to detect the active coding-agent harness based on project files so it installs to the right folder.
acceptanceCriteria: harness.rs exports enum Harness { ClaudeCode, Codex, OpenCode } and fn detect(project_root: &Path) -> Option<Harness>
Detection priority (first match wins): CLAUDE.md OR .claude/ -> ClaudeCode; AGENTS.md OR .codex/ -> Codex; opencode.json(c) OR .opencode/ -> OpenCode
Returns None if no signal matches
harness.target_folder() returns: ClaudeCode -> .claude/skills/; Codex -> .codex/skills/; OpenCode -> .opencode/skills/
harness.agents_md_file() returns: ClaudeCode -> CLAUDE.md; Codex -> AGENTS.md; OpenCode -> AGENTS.md
Unit tests cover all three positive cases, priority ordering when multiple signals coexist, and the None case
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)

userStories.title: Test infrastructure - mock HTTP and tempdir fake projects
userStories.description: As a developer, I want reusable test infrastructure so subsequent integration tests can run in isolation.

Helper module tests/common/mod.rs exposes: fake_claude_project() -> TempDir, fake_codex_project() -> TempDir, fake_opencode_project() -> TempDir

At least one smoke test uses each helper and passes
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Tests pass (cargo test)

userStories.title: HTTP layer downloading from GitHub Releases
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a centralized HTTP layer that downloads skill/snippet files from the registry's GitHub Releases so installation works in any environment.
acceptanceCriteria: http.rs uses ureq with rustls feature (smaller dep tree than reqwest)
Function download_release_asset(repo: &str, tag: &str, asset_name: &str) -> Result<Bytes> exists
Fetch URL: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset_name>
404 surfaces as 'asset not found' error; network failure as 'failed to reach github.com'
Tests use mock HTTP server from US-007 to verify success and 404 paths
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Tests pass

userStories.title: State file (.instinctagents) read/write
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a small state file in target projects so the tool knows what's installed without scanning the filesystem.
acceptanceCriteria: state.rs defines ProjectState { installed_skills: Vec<InstalledItem>, installed_agents_md: Vec<InstalledItem>, last_update_check: Option<DateTime<Utc>>, latest_known_version: Option<String> }
InstalledItem fields: name, version, source_url, install_path (skills) OR delimiter_id (agents.md, equal to skill name)
File format: TOML; path <project_root>/.instinctagents
ProjectState::load(project_root) returns default empty state if file missing
ProjectState::save(project_root) writes atomically (write to temp + rename)
Same file stores auto-update cache fields (last_update_check, latest_known_version)
Unit tests cover: load-missing, load-existing, save-and-roundtrip
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Tests pass

userStories.title: TUI scaffolding with tabs
userStories.description: As a user, I want a single TUI with tabs for Add / Remove / List / Update so I can do all operations from one interface.
acceptanceCriteria: ratatui used for full-screen TUI; crossterm for input
Four tabs: Add, Remove, List, Update; switchable with Tab / Shift+Tab or number keys 1-4
Header bar shows detected harness or warning 'No harness detected'; when no harness, Add and Remove are disabled

q or Esc exits cleanly with terminal state restored
Empty placeholder content in each tab is acceptable for this story
Integration test launches the binary, sends 'q', asserts exit code 0
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Manual verification in terminal (TUI is exception to dev-browser rule)

userStories.title: Inject agents.md snippet with delimiters
userStories.description: As a user, when I install an agents.md integration, the snippet must be injected into the project's harness instruction file with machine-parseable delimiters so it can be cleanly removed later.
acceptanceCriteria: Target file determined from harness.agents_md_file() (e.g. CLAUDE.md)
If target file does not exist, create it
Append to end of file (with one blank line before) using delimiters: <!-- instinctagents:start:<name> --> ... <!-- instinctagents:end:<name> -->
If a block with the same <name> already exists, replace it in place (no duplicate)
Never modify any content outside the delimiter pair
Update .instinctagents with new entry
Unit tests cover: fresh file, file with unrelated user content preserved verbatim, existing block of same name replaced, multiple existing blocks (only matching one affected)
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add tab - list, multi-select, install skills and agents.md
userStories.description: As a user, I want to browse the catalog in the Add tab and install one or more skills/snippets at once.
acceptanceCriteria: Two-section layout: skills section and agents.md integrations section
Each row shows: name, version, truncated description, harness-compat tag, [installed] marker if present in .instinctagents
Rows incompatible with detected harness are dimmed, not selectable, tagged like [claude-code only]
Space toggles selection (highlighted with checkmark)
Enter triggers installation for all checked items
If target install path already exists on disk, modal prompts Overwrite / Skip / Rename (default Skip when non-interactive)
Skill install: download tarball via US-008, extract to <harness_folder>/<skill_name>/, update .instinctagents
agents.md install delegates to US-011 logic
List refreshes to show [installed] markers after install
Errors shown inline as toast/footer message without crashing TUI
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Manual verification in terminal

userStories.title: Remove tab - list installed, multi-select, uninstall
userStories.description: As a user, I want a separate Remove tab that only shows what's currently installed in this project so I can uninstall items without distraction.
acceptanceCriteria: Reads .instinctagents; shows only entries from installed_skills and installed_agents_md
Empty state shows 'Nothing installed in this project.'
Multi-select with Space; confirm with Enter
Skill removal deletes the skill folder under <harness_folder>/<skill_name>/ and removes entry from .instinctagents
agents.md removal deletes the delimited block (inclusive) from the harness instruction file and removes entry from .instinctagents
If matching delimiter pair is missing, log a warning and still remove from .instinctagents
Confirmation modal before destructive action: 'Remove N item(s)? [y/N]'
Unit tests cover successful removal, missing-delimiter case, partial-state edges
Typecheck passes (cargo clippy -- -D warnings)
Manual verification in terminal

userStories.title: List tab - show what's installed

acceptanceCriteria: Two sections: 'Skills' and 'agents.md integrations'
Each entry shows: name, version, source_url, install_path
Empty state shows 'Nothing installed.'
Purely read-only (no editing)

Manual verification in terminal

userStories.title: Update tab - check binary for new version

userStories.title: CLI argument parsing with clap

Tests pass

userStories.title: Single-command curl install script

userStories.title: Integration tests - install/remove for all three harnesses

cargo test runs all tests green

userStories.title: skill-add script - ingest a skill from a URL
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a script that accepts a GitHub URL (repo, folder, or single file), downloads the contents, and adds them to skills/ in this registry repo.
acceptanceCriteria: Input: one positional URL argument
Repo root URL detection: fetch top-level tree via GitHub API; if single skill folder found (folder with SKILL.md or manifest.yml) import it; if multiple, prompt user to pick one
Folder URL detection (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<ref>/<path>): import as single skill
Raw file URL detection (blob URL or raw.githubusercontent.com): download single file, prompt: skill / agents.md / both
Imported skill goes to skills/<name>/ (name from source folder or sanitized filename)
If manifest.yml missing in source, scaffold one (prompt for description and version)
Update mapping.yml with new entry (name, version, source_url, install_path)
Refuse to overwrite existing entry without --force
Print confirmation summary of files added
Typecheck passes (python -m py_compile)

userStories.title: Release asset packaging script
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a reproducible step in the release workflow that packages each skill and agents.md integration into a tarball.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/package-release-assets.sh walks skills/ and agents.md/, reads each manifest.yml for version
Emits dist/skill-<name>-<version>.tar.gz and dist/agents-md-<name>-<version>.tar.gz
Tarball contents: entire folder rooted at the skill/integration name (extracting skill-foo-1.0.0.tar.gz produces foo/ directory)
Script deterministic: tar --sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime='1970-01-01'
Shell test runs the script against the repo and asserts expected tarballs are produced for example entries from US-001
shellcheck is clean
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: GitHub Actions release workflow - build and publish binary
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want pushing a v* git tag to build the Linux x86_64 binary and attach it to a GitHub release.
acceptanceCriteria: .github/workflows/release.yml triggers on tags matching v*.*.*
Job runs on ubuntu-latest with target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
Steps: checkout, install Rust stable + target, cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, strip binary, rename to instinctagents-linux-x86_64
Runs scripts/package-release-assets.sh (from US-029) before release step
Creates GitHub Release for the tag using softprops/action-gh-release or equivalent
Attaches instinctagents-linux-x86_64 and all tarballs from dist/ as release assets
Release notes auto-generated from commits since previous tag
Manual verification: tag v0.1.0, observe release created with all assets attached
